mentions.name: Trilogy typed SQL engine
mentions.description: A typed SQL engine. The author applies agent-assisted Lean formalization alongside previous fuzz coverage to surface untested case interactions and flush out null behavior in the engine.
mentions.problem: Edge-case interactions and null behavior in the SQL engine that had not yet been encountered in the wild.
mentions.source_excerpt: Late the bandwagon but have been experimenting with agent assisted lean/formalization for the first time; it's been surprisingly high ROI vs previous fuzz coverage and has forced me to think through some interactions of cases that  I hadn't yet encountered in the wild. Very useful for flushing out null behavior in my typed SQL engine [1].

mentions.name: Trilogy
mentions.description: Trilogy is a typed SQL language with composable functions of arbitrary complexity and a native semantic layer. Current work optimizes how well AI agents work with the language, achieving a 2-3x higher success rate and significantly lower total token usage on complex tasks, with the agent-focused design changes also measurably improving ergonomics for human users.
mentions.problem: AI agents have low success rates and high token consumption when working with a new language on complex tasks, and the language's initial syntax dump is currently rough and needs reduction via ablation.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Same as last month for once - optimizing how well agents can work with a new language [1]. I've been able to 2-3x success rate and drop total tokens for complex tasks significantly (though the initial syntax dump is rough - need to do some ablation there to get it down).

The best part has been that I think it's significantly improved things for humans too; it's weirdly satisfying to be able to measure improved ergonomics. Also, since a big pitch/theory was that the language should be ideal for agents as a result of the original nice things for humans it was designed for, it's a relief to be able actually measure a concrete lift.

[1] https://trilogydata.dev/ - SQL with types, composable functions of arbitrary complexity, and a native semantic layer.
